answer: Each agent identity must lock a slashable bond before earning fees, while randomly selected peers with established reputation audit its transactions for duplicated behavior, shared control, or impossible claims. Creating a hundred fake identities therefore requires a hundred separate bonds; coordinating them also creates detectable correlations. Once one is exposed, its bond is confiscated and its accounts lose future access, so the attacker pays real capital for every voyage and cannot cheaply hide a hollow cluster below the trust ledge.
